q: These time I agree for them to visit as a test trial because they insisted to help out with the baby after birth. I already hired a day time and night time doula but thought it would be nice to have someone watch the little one so me and husband can get a short break once a while. As I expected, the trial does not go well.
cx: Her parents stayed two months before the birth as a trial run for helping afterwards.

q: They also broke the garbage disposal, ripped off one of our cabinet doors and chipped paints in the living room which now I have to hire someone to fix. My dad constantly complains about things I purchase for home even though I am not spending his money. He even ask me why I need to purchase a crib for the baby lol..
cx: What the trial visit cost her.

q: Initially they wanted to stay till my due date. But after I made it clear this is not working out, they proposed to leave but want to return in September. I started to feel I am not going to get the help I want just based on my experience now.
cx: Deciding whether to let her parents return after the birth.

q: I’ve tried to return to the workforce but it’s been very difficult to find a job. And now that I’m pregnant we both feel weird about me getting a job because then I’ll just have to take off once the baby comes.
cx: First pregnancy; out of the military two years, building a slow business, husband works 40-60 hours.

q: I don’t agree with all these people saying “trust me, he’s glad he gets to go to work”. I can tell you my husband will absolutely not be happier going to work than staying at home with our new baby.
cx: Answering commenters about her husband missing time with the baby.

q: We are attending a birth class together soon so I’m hoping that will help him but I just fear worrying about him while I’m in labor. He doesn’t want to watch “the action” or cut the cord which is totally fine, and if he faints he faints, but I don’t think he’s emotionally prepared for how intense it could get.
cx: At 32 weeks her biggest worry is her husband's stress during labour.

q: She’s already mentioned that once my husband goes back to work, she could come over to help most days, or I could go to hers. She also mentioned wanting to be at the hospital when I give birth to help with parking (??).
cx: UK, nearly due; a loving mother-in-law 15 minutes away texts daily.

q: I work a physical job, I’m nearly due, exhausted, and genuinely only have one full day off a week. Seeing people takes effort right now.
cx: Why visits have thinned out late in pregnancy.

q: I appreciate I will need help and support but I also have many friends due the same time as me, my mum is coming to help, my sister will also have time off and my husband has a good 6 weeks off.
cx: Her help plan for after the birth, already in place.

q: Going to encourage my husband to inform her we will be birthing just the two of us and will need time at home before visitors arrive, he’s believing it’s best to tell her that after the birth but I think it’s best to clear it up now.
cx: When to tell family the visit plan.

q: I have a feeling in response to this she may say ‘oh you’ll want company and help as soon as she is here’ or ‘you’ll probably want visitors’
cx: The line she expects back when she sets the plan.

q: I just don't want this to be another instance where we're footing the bill and feeling used. It's only fair to say we split the cost 3 ways right?
cx: A stepmother asked to co-plan her stepdaughter's shower with two other mothers.

q: My MIL told us they will be coming over for 8-9 days and selected the dates. The dates were not discussed with us and she never asked if it was okay to stay, if we are comfortable with the length of stay, or any question that would allow us to communicate what we need.
cx: First baby due mid-June; out-of-state in-laws planned to stay a week and a half after the birth.

q: I would feel like a guest in my own house if my in laws were over that long and that soon post partum. […] Postpartum is not a time for me to experiment and see if the people who I have doubts about will step up to the plate.
cx: Why she said no to overnight guests in the newborn weeks.

q: I have observed that grandparents today relish in the title and do not know what help looks like.
cx: Her read on the in-laws' plan.

q: I had tears in my eyes going back after my short paternity leave. I genuinely didn’t want to leave her.
cx: A father back at work days into his daughter's life. No replies from the author.

q: I have a client with newborn preemie twins. MIL was absolutely sure they didn’t need to hire me as “she can handle it all”. Guess what. She can’t.
cx: A postpartum doula and new mother warns that family help isn't always help (self-interested source).

q: Now as a new father I have some fears only because I have no idea what to prepare, need and do so please any ideas would be amazing!
cx: US expectant father, baby due December, working double shifts; asks strangers for a full plan.

q: what things do I need to prepare? for example, I need to bring a car seat? (what kind, any recommendations?) also a blanket, clothes, some heating bottle, seperate laundry machine (like camping ones for baby clothes only) a list would be helpful and any specific name of item would be awesome!
cx: One of six numbered questions about birth and the hospital.

q: do we go to the hospital a day earlier or something or would that cost too much and they only accept like it's happening now type of situation? nothing like staying there 3 days earlier or sometjing? we are on medicaid.
cx: Not knowing how admission works or what it costs.

q: guilty as charged, movies is the reason the fears exist, especially when they have to give birth at home right after the water broke 😭 I will definitely look at local classes and library on books
cx: After replies suggest hospital tours, classes and books.

q: Now I am going back to work part time and using my remaining PTO intermittently to extend my paternity leave. I have a pretty demanding corporate role so even though I can work from home for these days its not like my company is condensing their needs down to 16 hours a week for my benefit.
cx: Father of a 3-week-old and an almost-3-year-old stretches leave with holiday days.

q: We kept him home from daycare for the first two weeks so I was mostly just supporting mom however I could between or during feedings and then keeping our toddler entertained while taking care of all the housework.
cx: How the couple handled the toddler in the first weeks with baby two.
